Bongani Lodge Fire

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A poacher dies from his wounds during a shootout with the Mthethomushahe anti-poaching unit - this led to the local village seeking revenge by setting the bongani luxury lodge on fire.

Unique Selling Point:
But there are questions whether the shootout ever happened according to the APU unit and the Mpumalanga tourism and parks agency or MTPA. The community, including the local chief Siyabonga Nkosi and community leaders are split. Some say there was a shooting, in which a man died, and others say there wasn't. But what is clear is that the night after the shooting the APU units had to defend the park from angry villagers all night, until all their shells were spent. Unable to defend the park any longer, they fled. Then the funeral of the man happened, and funeral goers spoke of burning down aha Bongani Mountain Lodge - the lodge that is located on the MTMA reserves land. Steffen Schneier its director managed to get everyone out, and by Sunday the entire lodge estimated at R80 million had burned to the ground.

Summary:
We speak to all involved. Including the SAPS - Leonard Hlathi who are hot on the heels of the perpetrators - they have made three arrests in a sting operation and will speak with us about what happened and how it led to their arrests. We are also going to go to the village and speak with the people there, meet the man who died's family and hear what they have to say. The situation is tense, but all involved are willing to speak and we will unravel what happened.

Further information:
Date: 08 February 2021

THREE MEN ARE DUE TO APPEAR IN COURT FOR ARSON AND OTHER CRIMES RELATING TO THE DAMAGED LODGE

NELSPRUIT - Three suspects aged between 28 and 37 are due to appear before the Kanyamazane Magistrate’s Court tomorrow, Tuesday 09 February 2021, for arson, possession of stolen goods and other crimes. Their appearance stems from an incident that occurred on 31 January 2021, where the Bongani Mountain Game Lodge, situated at Mthethomusha Game Reserve which borders on the Kruger National Park and shares a fence line with the Park came under attack.

On that day, a group of people driving in a white SUV alighted at the entrance of the said lodge. It is said that they then used rubble including stones and branches of trees to barricade the road which leads to the said lodge. Police were called to diffuse the situation, however while they were still clearing the road, other people amongst the group, proceeded to the lodge where they are reported to have broken several doors and helped themselves to liquor as well as other items belonging to the lodge. They also damaged some property as well, torching some of the rooms and other infrastructure before fleeing the scene with the stolen items, leaving behind a trail of costly damages of approximately R9 Million. Employees at the lodge reportedly had to run for their safety as they witnessed the horrific event unfolding in front of their eyes.

Police as well as other emergency personnel including the fire brigade responded to the scene and the blazing fire was extinguished.

Subsequent to this unpalatable event, a case of arson was registered with additional charges including theft, malicious damage to property, as well as public violence and a manhunt was then launched.

Police then received information pertaining to the case hence they traced and apprehended the trio. During their apprehension, one of the suspects was reportedly found in possession of certain items believed to have been stolen from the lodge.

Yesterday, Sunday, 07 February 2021, police received information of illegal porching that took place in the game reserve where the lodge is situated. They then responded promptly and together with the rangers, they discovered nine carcasses of four different animal species, including three Impala, four Inyala, one Rock Jumper and one Spoted Geanet.

A preliminary probe suggests that the carcasses were abandoned by a group of unscrupulous individuals who were involved in an illegal poaching activity earlier at the game reserve but were somehow given no chance through the visibility of the rangers which undoubtedly forced them to flee the scene, leaving behind their loot. At the same scene, police confiscated other items such as knives, pots and torches.

A case of illegal hunting was registered with the mentioned items seized and a manhunt has been motioned for the suspects. They (police) are following some positive leads in their investigation and are optimistic that arrests are eminent.

However, they also request the community to participate in the investigation, therefore anyone with tangible information pertaining to the said cases, should contact Detective Captain Vusimuzi Thobela at 082 469 1956, or call the Crime Stop number on 08600 10111. Alternatively members of the public can send information via MYSAPSAPP.

Police are also aware of the social media messages vigorously making rounds depicting that some members were reluctant in attending to the torching of the lodge, in that regard, an investigation has been launched. They (police) are also investigating a murder case involving a man who was found dead in his house at Matsulu near Nelspruit.

Script:



Nestled in the Mpumalanga mountains is the 8000 hectare Mthethomusha reserve which shares a border with the Kruger National Park. Inside the reserve is the exclusive Bongani Mountain Lodge - about R5,000 a night per room… but that was until a month ago when it was purposefully set alight by a crowd of angry villagers.
SO WHAT LED TO THIS EXCLUSIVE LODGE BEING BURNED TO THE GROUND? WELL IT ALLEGEDLY BEGAN WITH A COMMUNITY MEMBER BEING SHOT BY AN ANTI-POACHING UNIT AND LATER DIED BUT WHAT REALLY HAPPENED?
Thursday 28 January…title It all began 4 days before the fire when suspected poacher and Mpakeni villager Bekhumuzi Ngomane was murdered. Mpumalanga police spokesperson Brig. Leonard Hlathi says the community blames the reserve for the death.
Hlathi: All what we know is that he was found dead in his yard. Well, the narrative that we have drawn from the community is that they are alleging that the person who died, was allegedly killed by the Rangers here.
The community’s reaction goes to the heart of the conflict and mistrust that characterises the often fraught relationships between stakeholders in this piece of land. The plush Lodge is built on land that belongs to several neighbouring communities including Mpakeni. It is allowed to operate here thanks to two leases signed in the 1990s.Local traditional leadership leases the land to the Mpumalanga Tourism and Parks Agency or MTPA, which is responsible for protecting wildlife. The MTPA in turn leases the land to Bongani Mountain Lodge in return for a share of its earnings.The MTPA pays the local community the value of 10-12 buffalo per year, valued at R15 000 each. This money flows to the community through the Mpakeni Development Trust or MDT.
THE COMMUNITY IS SPLIT: ON THE ONE SIDE AN AGGRIEVED COMMUNITY WHO BELIEVE THE TOURISM AGENCIES AND LOCAL LODGES ARE NOT CREATING JOBS AND UPHOLDING THEIR SIDE OF THE LAND LEASE AGREEMENTS AND THEN THERE’S THE COMMUNITY MEMBERS WHO HAVE BENEFITTED FROM THE BONGANI LODGE – AND FEEL THE TOURISM INDUSTRY CREATES JOBS.
Local tour operator Bonginkosi Mbuyane says some parts of the community have been unhappy with this arrangement for a long time - for a myriad of reasons ranging from wild animals eating livestock because the reserves fences are down to a lack of financial opportunities offered to the community.
B: there are no like a proper tourism inclusion programs where people can benefit or can actually interact with the tourism industry, people have been disconnected completely from the industry.
Community leader Fanikie Mlombo says the community doesn’t trust the financial arrangements of the lease, and says there has been no transparency from the Trust.
F: They were supposed to come to the community as they are representing us to give us the report of how the money was spent for each year and things that they should be doing for us as we the beneficiaries.
Chief: From the side of the trust I think we have done little in terms of reporting to the people.
Chief Sicelo Nkosi, who chairs the Trust, agrees that the community has reason to be dissatisfied, saying that the Trust’s money goes to administration fees, as well as university bursaries.
Chief: I think about seven kids we appointed went to the University, so they are done now. They’re back. So we have some more money.
But Nkosi says the problem also lies with the structure of the 99 year lease itself, which he says is too long, outdated and undervalued. Boy Nobunga who's been the CEO of the MTPA for 4 years blames the Lodge for failing to uphold its side of the bargain and pay rent to the MTPA.
Nobunga: There hasn't been something flowing for the period I have been here.
But lodge director Steffen Schneier, one of 5 owners, says the lodge has spent 14 million rand on upkeep that was actually the MTPA’s responsibility.
The MTPA failed to do what they were required to do in the lease. And that runs at a budget of approximately one hundred thousand a month and that they set off against what was being paid to the MTPA.
The MTPA says the agreement is unfair. The Chief, meanwhile, supports the lodge as it has paid R3.7 million to several community education initiatives.
Steff: We had fifty five accepted into university and getting NSF funding, which for a group of rural villages is actually quite extraordinary.
The lodge also created 80 -100 permanent jobs from hotel staff, to rangers, drivers and security. It’s a complicated arrangement that has caused tension for years...tension that came to a violent head after Ngomane’s death in January.
Friday 30 January…title… The evening following Ngomane’s death, around 30 members of the Mpakeni community allegedly attacked the reserve’s ranger station.
Some members of the community went into the reserve, they then attacked our property or infrastructure, they attacked our offices, they attacked the principal by the house.
LINK: THEY CAME HERE AND THE RANGERS TRIED TO DEFEND THIS PLACE FROM ABOUT 8PM RIGHT UP UNTIL THE MORNING, THEY ONLY LEFT WHEN THEY RAN OUT OF BULLETS AND THAT’S WHEN THE VILLAGERS THEN BREACHED THE AREA.
shoba: they were coming to actually attack us in revenge
The MTPA’s Boniwe Shoba manages the rangers near Mpakeni.
Mac: Do your Rangers know anything about this? Were they involved in it?
B: They were actually not involved in this shooting. That is actually that which they are telling us when we interviewed them.
It was at this time that Schneier, became aware of the threat to the lodge.
Saturday 31 January…title And so we started hearing the rumors, I believe, on Saturday that there was going to be an attack on the lodge. The commander of the pienaar station He was advised that the police would be at the gate, that they would establish a presence.
Sunday 1 February… title Steff: Later on the Sunday, there was definitely going to be an attack.
The group then travelled 15km in broad daylight, and while police waited for backup, the lodge was left defenseless.
Hlathi: We had to clear the road first. This situation developed into a protest because they barricaded off roads with stones.
Steff: luckily we abandoned the lodge in time, literally. I was speaking to one of the staff members who was told, get everything that's in your staff room. You've got 20 minutes to evacuate.
Over the next several hours – the lodge turned to ash. (Fade to black)
The majority of the people are really disappointed the lodge is closed.
Some believe the community's reputation has been irreversibly damaged by the burning of the lodge, but Mbuyane says the arsonists don’t represent the views of the whole community. Mlombo believes some community members mistakenly believed the reserve and the lodge were the same entity, which may explain why they attacked the lodge in revenge for Ngomane’s death.
We can’t stop people from getting into the game reserve, because people say ‘’the game reserve is not helping them with anything anyway, they only took our land’’
The damage amounts to roughly R60 million, but the lodge’s owners haven’t decided whether or not to rebuild.
It's very hard to. We truly believe that we made a difference and that we behaved in a manner that was very respectful. Towards the surrounding communities, we found it very complicated terrain because there are many different agendas but there was an enormous amount that we were held responsible for in a sense, over which we had no control.
Meanwhile, in an ironic twist, new evidence now suggests Ngomane wasn’t shot by rangers and perhaps the villagers’ anger was misplaced.
Nobunga: The postmortem report currently indicates the victim did not die from an R1 Rifle, which is a machine gun that our Rangers are using. They are saying it is from a pistol.
Mac: So from your understanding, this was a fire fight between two rival poaching gangs?
Boy: That's the report we have got.
WE TRIED TO SPEAK TO THE FAMILY OF BEKHUMUZI NGOMANE BUT HIS FATHER DECLINED AS THE FAMILY ARE STILL IN MOURNING, AND IT’S NOT YET CLEAR WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED WHETHER HIS SON IS ACTUALLY A POACHER, BUT WE CAN ONLY GET THAT INFORMATION WHEN POLICE HAVE DONE THEIR WORK AND THERE’S EVIDENCE TO PROVE THAT.
Three suspects were arrested and appeared in the Kanyamazane Court on charges of arson, possession of stolen goods and other crimes.
SAPS: As I'm talking to you right now, there's also a sting operation that is in motion.
That same day another two suspects were arrested. In the meantime, vulnerable game like rhino have been moved to a secret location and the MTPA is hoping to find a resolution to the tensions that continue to bubble in this community.
Nobunga: We're currently working together with the chief to try and reform the MDT.
Bonginkosi: it is not alone charity and handouts that will change the conditions of the indigents. We need to not to speak salary alone. We also need to speak profit. We need to find programs where people can make profit out of the industry so they can have a particular type of ownership. 10.08

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A poacher dies from his wounds during a shootout with the Mthethomushahe anti-poaching unit - this led to the local village seeking revenge by setting the bongani luxury lodge on fire.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: But there are questions whether the shootout ever happened according to the APU unit and the Mpumalanga tourism and parks agency or MTPA. The community, including the local chief Siyabonga Nkosi and community leaders are split. Some say there was a shooting, in which a man died, and others say there wasn't. But what is clear is that the night after the shooting the APU units had to defend the park from angry villagers all night, until all their shells were spent. Unable to defend the park any longer, they fled. Then the funeral of the man happened, and funeral goers spoke of burning down aha Bongani Mountain Lodge - the lodge that is located on the MTMA reserves land. Steffen Schneier its director managed to get everyone out, and by Sunday the entire lodge estimated at R80 million had burned to the ground.
metadata.Summary: We speak to all involved. Including the SAPS - Leonard Hlathi who are hot on the heels of the perpetrators - they have made three arrests in a sting operation and will speak with us about what happened and how it led to their arrests. We are also going to go to the village and speak with the people there, meet the man who died's family and hear what they have to say. The situation is tense, but all involved are willing to speak and we will unravel what happened.
metadata.Further information: Date: 08 February 2021 THREE MEN ARE DUE TO APPEAR IN COURT FOR ARSON AND OTHER CRIMES RELATING TO THE DAMAGED LODGE NELSPRUIT - Three suspects aged between 28 and 37 are due to appear before the Kanyamazane Magistrate’s Court tomorrow, Tuesday 09 February 2021, for arson, possession of stolen goods and other crimes. Their appearance stems from an incident that occurred on 31 January 2021, where the Bongani Mountain Game Lodge, situated at Mthethomusha Game Reserve which borders on the Kruger National Park and shares a fence line with the Park came under attack. On that day, a group of people driving in a white SUV alighted at the entrance of the said lodge. It is said that they then used rubble including stones and branches of trees to barricade the road which leads to the said lodge. Police were called to diffuse the situation, however while they were still clearing the road, other people amongst the group, proceeded to the lodge where they are reported to have broken several doors and helped themselves to liquor as well as other items belonging to the lodge. They also damaged some property as well, torching some of the rooms and other infrastructure before fleeing the scene with the stolen items, leaving behind a trail of costly damages of approximately R9 Million. Employees at the lodge reportedly had to run for their safety as they witnessed the horrific event unfolding in front of their eyes. Police as well as other emergency personnel including the fire brigade responded to the scene and the blazing fire was extinguished. Subsequent to this unpalatable event, a case of arson was registered with additional charges including theft, malicious damage to property, as well as public violence and a manhunt was then launched. Police then received information pertaining to the case hence they traced and apprehended the trio. During their apprehension, one of the suspects was reportedly found in possession of certain items believed to have been stolen from the lodge. Yesterday, Sunday, 07 February 2021, police received information of illegal porching that took place in the game reserve where the lodge is situated. They then responded promptly and together with the rangers, they discovered nine carcasses of four different animal species, including three Impala, four Inyala, one Rock Jumper and one Spoted Geanet. A preliminary probe suggests that the carcasses were abandoned by a group of unscrupulous individuals who were involved in an illegal poaching activity earlier at the game reserve but were somehow given no chance through the visibility of the rangers which undoubtedly forced them to flee the scene, leaving behind their loot. At the same scene, police confiscated other items such as knives, pots and torches. A case of illegal hunting was registered with the mentioned items seized and a manhunt has been motioned for the suspects. They (police) are following some positive leads in their investigation and are optimistic that arrests are eminent. However, they also request the community to participate in the investigation, therefore anyone with tangible information pertaining to the said cases, should contact Detective Captain Vusimuzi Thobela at 082 469 1956, or call the Crime Stop number on 08600 10111. Alternatively members of the public can send information via MYSAPSAPP. Police are also aware of the social media messages vigorously making rounds depicting that some members were reluctant in attending to the torching of the lodge, in that regard, an investigation has been launched. They (police) are also investigating a murder case involving a man who was found dead in his house at Matsulu near Nelspruit.
